source_snapshot.purpose_facts: Use the AMD RAS error-injection tool to inject a DRAM uncorrectable fatal condition across memory slots 1~N, obtain tool PASS and OS evidence within a timeout, and observe the specified shutdown and restart.
procedure_facts: Verify configuration and establish a log boundary.
Apply the listed DRAM and MCA setting blocks, including conflicting values for DRAM Corrected Error Counter Enable.
Unlock the CPU via HDT and boot Ubuntu 20.04, RHEL 9.0 or Windows Server 2022.
List valid UMCs, then run one fixed-address `--einjdramecc --address 0x1000 --address_mask 0xffffffffffffffc0 --enablemcapolling 0 --errortype 2` command.
criteria_facts: The tool reports PASS for the uncorrectable error.
The OS reports the error within a defined timeout.
Validate dmesg and the injection report against the AMD RAS specification.
The system shuts down and restarts.
source_conflicts: The DRAM block sets `DRAM Corrected Error Counter Enable` to NoLeakMode while the MCA block sets the same option to Disabled, but the source does not say whether these are alternatives or separate phases.
The source permits Linux or Windows Server 2022 but the criteria universally require dmesg, which does not apply to Windows.
The title requires memory slots 1~N, but the procedure provides one fixed address/mask and no address-to-UMC/channel/DIMM/slot mapping or iteration.
missing_source_information: N and the per-slot physical/logical memory map.
Whether DRAM and MCA setting blocks are alternatives, sequential phases or an editorial merge.
Per-slot injectable address/mask derivation and proof that the address belongs to the target slot.
OS-specific evidence path and timeout value.
Exact expected shutdown versus reset/restart sequence and recovery limits.

original_test_intent.statement: Validate AMD DRAM uncorrectable fatal-error handling for every required memory slot using a platform-approved injection address and profile, including timely OS reporting, tool PASS and the expected controlled shutdown/restart path.
must_preserve: AMD memory-slot 1~N scope and fatal uncorrectable severity.
The exact source command shape with `errortype 2` and `enablemcapolling 0`, but only after address validation.
Supported OS choice without mixing evidence between OSes.
Tool PASS, OS report within timeout and shutdown/restart as separate acceptance conditions.
must_not_infer: That address 0x1000 maps to every slot or even to an injectable target on the selected platform.
That the conflicting DRAM and MCA setting blocks can be applied together.
That Linux dmesg/rasdaemon is available on Windows.
That a process PASS before shutdown proves slot coverage, fatal handling, restart or post-boot health.

v2_review_conclusion.summary: V2 retains a gated hybrid, recognizes fatal reset risk and requires a valid UMC/address recipe, HDT, tool evidence and recovery.
v2_review_conclusion.specific_gap: V2 repeats the fixed 0x1000 command while claiming slot/UMC targeting, tells the operator to apply both contradictory profiles, and requires dmesg/rasdaemon without branching for the allowed Windows execution.

related_records: Same-title Intel correctable and AMD correctable/non-fatal/fatal/implicit/parity rows are separate variants and cannot supply this fatal recipe.
applicable_history.precedence_application: The exact row fixes AMD fatal severity, but its internal contradictions require owner resolution rather than borrowing an adjacent recipe.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Retain the gated hybrid capability but prohibit injection until the owner resolves the contradictory BIOS profiles, defines one OS-specific evidence branch and supplies a per-slot injectable-address matrix. Safe inventory and baseline collection may proceed.

conditions_present: The intended AMD fatal DRAM fault class, candidate tool invocation, supported OS choices and top-level shutdown/restart criteria are known.
missing: Resolved BIOS profile/phases; complete slot/UMC/channel/DIMM/address map; exact tool build; OS-specific event path; timeout and power-transition timeline; approvals, recovery and final-state rules.
provider: Test owner resolves the two setting blocks and selects the OS evidence branch.
AMD/ODM FAE supplies the signed tool/address/severity recipe and expected event/reset behavior.
Platform owner supplies the physical memory topology and per-slot address mapping; lab owner supplies approval and recovery.
safe_read_only_work: Inventory CPU/UMC/channel/DIMM/slot/SPD/serial, BIOS/BMC/OS versions and current settings.
Run `--listvalidumc` only if the signed tool documentation confirms that operation is non-mutating.
Export existing OS-native, BMC and firmware records and verify console/OOB/recovery readiness without clearing or injecting.
prohibited_until_resolved: Changing either BIOS profile, HDT unlock, tool injection, log clear, deliberate shutdown/reset, power cycle, retry or restoration.
closure_evidence: Owner-signed profile states one configuration or explicit isolated phases and resolves the conflicting option.
Each required slot has a validated UMC/channel/DIMM/physical-slot/address/mask tuple.
Selected OS has a native evidence query, timeout, expected fatal/power sequence and approved recovery/restoration plan.

revision_candidate.test_name: AMD DRAM Fatal UE Injection Across Memory Slots 1~N
revision_candidate.purpose: For every required physical memory slot, inject one approved AMD DRAM uncorrectable fatal error at an address proven to map to that slot and verify tool completion, timely native-OS reporting, the expected shutdown/restart sequence and post-recovery health.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Only the AMD platform/stepping, BIOS/BMC/firmware, ECC DIMM population, selected Ubuntu 20.04, RHEL 9.0 or Windows Server 2022 branch, HDT method and AMD RAS tool build covered by the signed recipe.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Every populated and explicitly required memory slot 1~N in the signed matrix, sequentially. Each row binds socket/die/UMC/channel/DIMM/rank/physical label/serial to one verified injectable address and mask. Exclude correctable, non-fatal, Intel, implicit and parity variants. Treat 60/120 minutes as estimates.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: N and signed physical/logical slot plus address/mask matrix; owner-resolved DRAM-versus-MCA BIOS profile or separated phases; AMD RAS tool build/hash and `errortype 2` semantics; HDT procedure; selected OS-native event query; timeout; expected shutdown/power-off/restart timeline; BMC/firmware expectations; per-slot go/no-go; approval, recovery and final-state plan.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Preserve and hash OS-native, BMC and firmware baselines before any approved clear or establish a timestamp marker. A qualified operator applies exactly the resolved BIOS profile for the current phase, performs approved HDT unlock and boots one selected OS. Verify tool/package identity, `--listvalidumc` and the current slot's address tuple. After per-slot authorization, execute one exact `--einjdramecc --address <signed_address> --address_mask <signed_mask> --enablemcapolling 0 --errortype 2` invocation, preserve the full report and record OS event and power-transition timing through the expected shutdown/restart. After recovery, collect health/restoration evidence before any next slot.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Source conflicts resolved; exact platform/population/profile/tool/address/OS branch approved; dedicated idle non-production SUT; per-slot backups and evidence storage; synchronized clocks; console/OOB and automatic/manual recovery behavior proven; qualified observer; all BIOS, unlock, clear, injection, power, recovery and restoration approvals recorded.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Platform/tool identities and hashes; signed slot-address/profile matrix; DIMM SPD/part/serial and topology; BIOS before/during/after; baseline/clear audit; valid-UMC output; exact per-slot command and complete tool report containing PASS; selected OS-native fatal record tied to expected UMC/address within the signed timeout; BMC/firmware/power-state timeline; shutdown and restart evidence; post-boot inventory/memory/health, anomalies, recovery and restored final state.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The exact AMD/ODM fatal DRAM injection specification and owner-resolved platform profile. Each slot independently requires the tool PASS, its native OS error within the approved timeout, the specified shutdown/restart transition and healthy restoration; none substitutes for another.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Critical fatal memory injection on a dedicated SUT only. Do not combine contradictory BIOS values, guess addresses or slot mapping, reuse adjacent severities, inject 0x1000 universally, mix Linux and Windows evidence, target production memory, expose secrets, truncate logs, auto-loop, interrupt an expected power transition, retry after failure or continue after wrong target/severity, error storm, no-boot or instability.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Test owner approves the resolved profile and OS branch; platform owner approves every slot/address tuple; AMD/ODM FAE approves tool/severity and expected power path; qualified operator performs BIOS/HDT and observes power/recovery. Every injection, next-slot go/no-go, exceptional recovery and restoration requires signed authorization.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Qualified staff own BIOS/HDT, physical slot confirmation, observation of shutdown/restart and exceptional recovery. After exact handoff, an authorized Agent may run the bounded tool command and collect/correlate native OS, OOB and power evidence; engineering retains anomaly and final PASS/FAIL judgment.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: On wrong slot/address/profile, missing tool PASS or native OS event, timeout, unexpected power state, repeated reset, no boot, persistent fatal state or memory loss, stop the matrix, preserve evidence, use only the approved OOB/platform recovery, disable injection/unlock state and restore the signed BIOS/profile before any separately approved rerun.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Unresolved profile or OS branch; missing/ambiguous slot-address map; tool/HDT/BIOS mismatch; missing approval, baseline, timeout, observer, recovery or evidence; invalid UMC/address; wrong target or severity; tool failure; absent/late OS event; unexpected or absent shutdown/restart; reboot loop/no-boot; persistent fatal record, DIMM loss, thermal/power/memory instability; or failed restoration/final health.

identified_defects: The source contains contradictory values for the same DRAM counter option without defining alternative or sequential profiles.
The single fixed address does not implement or prove memory-slot 1~N coverage.
The allowed Windows branch conflicts with universal dmesg acceptance criteria.
V2 tells the operator to apply both source profiles and repeats 0x1000 without resolving physical target mapping.
Tool PASS, OS timeout report and shutdown/restart are not explicitly kept as independent per-slot gates in V2.
reason_for_change: Prevent a fatal injection under contradictory firmware state or at an unverified address, while preserving full 1~N coverage and OS-specific evidence.

new_technical_evidence.title: Red Hat Enterprise Linux Tuning Guide for AMD EPYC 9005 Series Processors
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Public AMD Linux guidance illustrates address/mask-based memory injection; exact platform generation here remains unknown
new_technical_evidence.supports: AMD's published example requires a chosen memory address and mask and distinguishes simulated MCE from real hardware error-injection interfaces; a fixed address cannot be assumed to cover every DIMM slot.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: This source does not document the private tool build, errortype 2, the tested platform's decoding or the Windows branch.

new_technical_evidence.title: Linux Kernel: Error Detection And Correction Devices
new_technical_evidence.supports: EDAC reports memory error location and DIMM labels, so slot attribution requires a platform-specific mapping and raw location evidence.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: EDAC availability and label accuracy depend on the selected kernel/platform and do not apply to Windows.

new_technical_evidence.title: Source testcase Wistron-System RAS-00764-V002
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Only this AMD fatal memory-slot row
new_technical_evidence.supports: The conflicting BIOS blocks, three OS choices, fixed command and independent PASS/timeout/shutdown criteria.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Profile relationship, slot/address iteration and OS-native evidence are unresolved.

removed_ambiguities: Makes the contradictory profile a mandatory owner decision instead of silently combining it.
Requires one proven physical-slot/address tuple per 1~N target.
Separates Linux and Windows evidence branches.
Keeps tool PASS, OS reporting, shutdown/restart and final health as independent gates and excludes adjacent memory-fault variants.
resolved_blockers: The test remains technically automatable after platform/FAE inputs and manual setup; unresolved current readiness does not change capability to BLOCKED.
remaining_blockers: Execution is blocked by the contradictory profile, absent per-slot address matrix, unspecified OS-native evidence/timeout and incomplete power/recovery rules.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 exposes three source contradictions V2 carried into execution, prevents universal 0x1000 injection, and defines safe per-slot, per-OS fatal recovery evidence without weakening approval or recovery controls.

agent_understanding_result.notes: Contract-only validation recovered the unresolved DRAM/MCA profile conflict, one selected OS branch, one proven address/mask per signed slot, three independent tool/OS/power gates and sequential per-slot recovery. It rejected universal 0x1000, mixed-OS evidence, auto-looping and treating reboot as retroactive proof of a wrong target.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: Reliability row 44 runs AMD errortype-2 DRAM injection for Memory slot 1~N and requires tool PASS, timely OS reporting and shutdown/restart.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 correctly retains REQUIRES and fatal safety but silently combines conflicting profiles, repeats fixed 0x1000 and does not branch OS evidence.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Permit only inventory and approved non-mutating UMC/baseline work; forbid profile change, HDT and fatal injection until contradictions, address mapping and recovery are signed.
